title: CREATION CARE
mv: The earth is the LORD’s, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.
mvp: “The earth is the LORD’s, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.” Psalm 24:1
outline: Reality of Neglect and Personal Responsibility
assignment: Itemise five (5) activities you will engage in to promote creation care (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: The world today is groaning under the weight of environmental crises such as climate change, pollution, deforestation, and wastefulness. While governments and scientists struggle for solutions, the Bible reminds us that God placed man in charge of His creation, not to selfishly exploit it, but to care for it responsibly (Genesis 2:15). Creation care is not a modern idea; it is a biblical mandate.

God gave man dominion with responsibility (Genesis 1:26-28; Psalm 8:6-8). Dominion is not destruction, but stewardship. Humans are caretakers, not owners, because everything belongs to God, who upholds the principle of tending and keeping (Genesis 2:15, Psalm 24:1). God expects us to preserve, maintain, and protect resources. Our Lord Jesus dislikes waste (John 6:12).

On the contrary, man has not taken full control of caring for the creation entrusted to his care. The groaning of creation (Romans 8:19-22) is evident in pollution, natural disasters, drought, extinction of species and lots more. These are signs of a fallen world. Human carelessness accelerates the decay. Famines, floods, fire-outbreaks and extreme weather are reminders of the end (Matthew 24:6-7; Revelation 8:7-9). The earth reveals how much man has not been fully responsible in taking adequate care of what God has committed to him.

sections.h: REALITY OF NEGLECT AND PERSONAL RESPONSIBILITY

b.x: Consequences of neglect include a shortage of clean water and food insecurity; health challenges from pollution and poor sanitation. The spiritual implication is that careless stewardship will be judged (Luke 16:2). Therefore, everyone, including believers, has personal responsibilities to take over creation.

Avoid waste (food, energy, resources). Plant trees, care for animals, and manage waste properly. Also, teach children stewardship of creation; undertake community responsibility such as keeping neighbourhoods clean; participating in environmental initiatives; supporting sustainable practices (re-use, recycle, and reduce).

Spiritual responsibility includes living with the fear of God and having eternity in view in our dealings with nature (2 Peter 3:10-13); Using creation as a witness to God’s glory (Psalm 19:1-2), shining as examples in a careless world (Matthew 5:14-16). You must also realise that you are God’s creation and it is fundamental for you to take good care of yourself, i.e. your spirit, soul, and body (1 Thessalonians 5:23).
To neglect creation is to dishonour the Creator. As accountable believers, we must see creation care as both a spiritual duty and a Christian witness.

i: Explain God’s mandate on creation care.
Mention five ways believers can be responsible for creation.
